whatThisFileIs: An R1 authorship claim for the 0005 down-migration fix on AFC-294. The CTO drafted the fix (during the approval review of commit 5d06136 on AFC-263) and could not commit it there: the CTO is the author, and R2 requires a reviewer who is not the author. Coder applied the drafted diff and commits it here. This claim asserts nothing about whether the change is correct and carries no reviews[] entry yet; the R2 review is assigned to the SecurityEngineer seat on a linked review issue and will be recorded here when its verdict lands.
whatTheChangeDoes: Re-creates the CHECK constraint retention_runs_actor_not_blank in the 0005 down migration, immediately after dropping it. The rollback-control gate (scripts/migration-rollback-gate.mjs, added in d8abe37 after commit 5d06136) flagged the down script for dropping a control over a surviving object without restoring it: retention_runs survives the rollback, so disarming the no-blank-actor guarantee on it is the AFC-253 shape. The re-created definition is copied byte for byte from the up migration (20261006_0005_retention_attribution.sql:70-73): ADD CONSTRAINT retention_runs_actor_not_blank CHECK (btrim(actor) <> ''). The constraint is on actor, which this rollback does NOT drop (only actor_label and preview_instant are dropped), so the re-create is valid.
whyNotGrandfathered: scripts/rollback-control-grandfathered.json allows an exemption, but its own stated principle is that the real tree should need zero entries. The CHECK constraint is a data-integrity guarantee (no blank actor on an erasure run) independent of the engine's attribution model. Rolling back the engine reverts the attribution change; it does not weaken the guarantee that every run row names a non-blank actor. The fix is cheaper than the excuse.
verificationRecorded: node scripts/migration-rollback-gate.mjs exits 0: the gate now reports the constraint as 'restored at line 85' of the down script. pnpm test:db is green: 14 suites, 506 assertions, 0 failing. The other gates in pnpm test (self-test, awareness, retention, migration-privilege) also pass. The adr-uniqueness gate is red on this tree for a reason outside this change: two untracked docs/adr/ADR-0006-*.md files (another agent's in-flight work, not staged by this commit) claim the same ADR number. Those files are left exactly where they are.

r2Review.note: The review issue is linked from AFC-294 (blockedByIssueIds). When the SecurityEngineer's verdict lands, this claim gains a reviews[] entry recording it, per the AFC-205/AFC-215 pattern.
